verdict.rationale: Deepgram ships a first-party MCP server built into its dg CLI, so a user can drive Deepgram APIs with natural language through an AI coding tool. That is a real but indirect path: there is no native natural-language console or command interface for configuring or managing Voice Agents, and the evidence does not show the MCP server covers Voice Agent operations specifically. The agents' conversational ability serves end users on calls, not operators of the product. missing for 10: native natural-language control in the product itself, documented MCP coverage of Voice Agent configuration and management, hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: The dg CLI includes a built-in MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that gives AI coding tools direct access to Deepgram APIs.
